I farm the 6.0 mu as one wheat-maize rotation, so I will plant winter wheat on all 6.0 mu first and then summer maize on the same 6.0 mu after wheat harvest. I have farmed for 30 years and I have well irrigation, so I will stay with a steady, practical way that I know I can manage well with a two-person household. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put more nitrogen overall, add enough phosphorus for rooting, and keep potassium moderate. I will irrigate a few key times because water is available and wheat responds well. I will use rotary tillage because it is simpler and fits my scale. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because it gives me better yield on irrigated land. I will fertilize it a bit more heavily than wheat on nitrogen, keep phosphorus and potassium moderate, and irrigate in the important periods if rainfall is short. I will keep pesticide sprays limited but timely, because I do not want to spend more than needed, but I also do not want yield loss. My aim is stable grain output, manageable labor, and low risk.
